solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Partner beginning to hate The Eagles?

indicators.note: the opening of the word hate is all that is wanted from it here

parts.note: the Eagles are an American rock group, so a US band

explanation.surface: Someone's other half has just started to loathe a certain classic rock group.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that The Eagles is not birds but the Californian band, defined by example.
explanation.definitionFit: A spouse is a life partner, and a married man is the male partner.

clue.text: A TV Irish hotel replaced for nurse

indicators.note: the letters of a TV Irish hotel are put back in a new order

explanation.surface: A television in an Irish hotel has been swapped for a nurse.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain this is a community nurse who visits homes, especially new mothers and babies.

clue.text: Organisation with number mounting attack

parts.note: a setup is an arrangement or organisation

indicators.note: in a down clue, mounting means climbing, so the number is read bottom to top

explanation.surface: A group with a growing number of members launches an assault.
explanation.definitionFit: To set upon someone is to assault them, a phrasal verb meaning attack.

clue.text: Put to use couple of pages and line in a back of diary

indicators.note: the pages and line go inside the other letters
only the last letter of diary is taken

parts.note: PP is the abbreviation for pages

explanation.surface: Using two pages and a line at the back of a diary.
explanation.definitionFit: To apply a method or skill is to employ it, bring it into use.

clue.text: Discriminating place for foreign food and provision (not half)

parts.note: a deli or delicatessen sells imported specialities

indicators.note: the word loses its second half, keeping the first four letters

parts.note: catering is the provision of food

explanation.surface: A discerning delicatessen offering foreign fare, though only partly catering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not half' is also British slang for very much, which the surface plays on.
explanation.definitionFit: A delicate judgement is subtle and finely discerning, as a discriminating palate is.

clue.text: Pair of auxiliaries act correctly

parts.note: two auxiliary verbs of English: the first is the verb to be
the second of the two auxiliary verbs is the verb to have

explanation.surface: Two helpers on a team or ship conduct themselves properly.
explanation.definitionFit: To conduct oneself properly or with good manners is the everyday sense of the verb.

clue.text: Preserve courage

definitions.meaning: to store food in jars to keep it
British slang for nerve or guts

explanation.surface: Keep your nerve.
explanation.definitionFit: To put fruit into jars preserves it; in British slang, having nerve or daring is the second sense.

clue.text: Bigoted devotee defending limited plan by bishop

indicators.note: the devotee surrounds and so guards the other letters

parts.note: a hound is an enthusiast, as in a news hound

indicators.note: the plan is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: an idea is a plan
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A zealot protecting a narrow scheme put forward by a bishop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'devotee' is a fan, as in news hound; 'limited' trims the plan and 'defending' wraps it, with 'by' a mere joiner.
explanation.definitionFit: Narrow-minded and set in old ways, stubbornly prejudiced, as a bigot is.

clue.text: Abuse in Spanish city not good after hours

indicators.note: the letter for good is left out

parts.note: Vigo is a port in Galicia, Spain
late means after the usual time

explanation.surface: Misbehaviour in a Spanish city, no good after closing time.
explanation.definitionFit: To violate rights or a person is to abuse or mistreat them.

clue.text: Ideal place almost in a group for flight aid

indicators.note: the ideal place sits inside the phrase a group

parts.note: a lot is a set or batch of items

indicators.note: the last letter of the ideal place is dropped

parts.note: Utopia is the imagined perfect society of Thomas More

explanation.surface: A near-perfect spot within a crowd is somehow an aid to flying.
explanation.definitionFit: An automatic steering system keeps an aircraft on course, a help to the pilot in flight.

clue.text: Sad duke recalled in decline

indicators.note: called back, so the words sad duke are read from end to start

parts.note: poor can mean sorry or pitiable, a sense of sad

explanation.surface: An unhappy nobleman has been summoned back while his fortunes slump.
explanation.definitionFit: To sag or sink downwards, or to lose vigour, is to decline.

clue.text: Journalists with article on revolutionary writer start to hope to solicit support?

parts.note: the press is the body of journalists
the is the definite article

indicators.note: turning round, so the word for the writer is read backwards

parts.note: the setter calls themselves myself, the self who writes

indicators.note: only the opening letter of hope is used

explanation.surface: Reporters stirring up a radical author hoping to win backing.
explanation.definitionFit: Shaking hands with crowds, as politicians do while campaigning for votes.

clue.text: Untidy place steadily emptying is affected by drink

parts.note: a tip is a messy place, like a rubbish dump

indicators.note: removing the contents of steadily leaves only its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A messy flat whose occupant drains glass after glass is clearly under the influence.
explanation.definitionFit: Slightly drunk; mildly intoxicated by alcohol.

clue.text: Mark positions of a sign in ground etc

indicators.note: a sign is placed within the other letters
ground means crushed or pulverised, so the letters of etc are broken up

parts.note: Libra is a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: Instructions for marking where a symbol goes on a plot of land and so on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' is the past tense of grind, an anagram signal, not a plot of land; the scrambled etc splits to hold the sign.
explanation.definitionFit: To calibrate an instrument is to mark the graduations on its scale.

clue.text: Corruption? There's vital yen for reform

indicators.note: the words vital yen are to be reformed into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A vital appetite for reforming a corrupt system is a sign of graft, the clue asks.
explanation.definitionFit: Being open to bribery is the quality meant; venal officials are corruptible.

clue.text: Garland for certain befitting a holiday?

parts.note: a lei is a Hawaiian garland of flowers
surely means certainly

explanation.surface: A flower garland is undoubtedly right for a trip to Hawaii.
explanation.definitionFit: Relaxed and unhurried, the pace suited to leisure time off work.

clue.text: Constraint for all to see in outfit

indicators.note: the letter for all to see goes within the outfit

parts.note: a dress is an outfit
U is the British film certificate for universal viewing, suitable for everyone

explanation.surface: A restriction on what can be shown publicly in someone's clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the British cinema rating meaning a film is fit for all audiences.
explanation.definitionFit: Coercion or threats that compel someone to act form a constraint on them.

clue.text: Sweet temp's work ending in office

parts.note: a temp may serve as a personal assistant, so PA's
to till is to work the soil

indicators.note: only the final letter of office is taken

explanation.surface: A temporary worker's output finishing at the office, with sweets on the desk.
explanation.definitionFit: A small lozenge or fruit gum is a type of sweet or candy.

clue.text: Period for dealing with disorder?

parts.note: sounds like time for tackling unrest, but a disorder is an illness and the period a day off to recover

explanation.surface: A spell set aside for handling public unrest.
explanation.walkthrough: British slang for a day taken off work claiming illness, often when not really unwell.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal British word for a day's sick leave, time off for an ailment.

clue.text: Legal figure with circle entering predicament

indicators.note: the circle goes into the predicament

parts.note: a corner is a tight spot or predicament
O is shaped like a circle

explanation.surface: A lawyer drawing a ring lands in a fix.
explanation.definitionFit: An official who inquires into sudden deaths, a judicial officer.

clue.text: Brandish card when in mess — or ready money

indicators.note: the scrambled card is placed within the mess

parts.note: a hash is a mess or jumble

indicators.note: to brandish is to wave about, so the letters of card are thrown around

explanation.surface: Waving a card about in a muddle, or paying in banknotes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brandish' reads as a verb of display but signals the scramble; 'in' sets the result within the mess, 'when' and 'or' are joiners.
explanation.definitionFit: Ready money is cash in hand, notes and coins rather than credit.

clue.text: US state region largely featuring in part of opera

indicators.note: the region appears inside the opera part

parts.note: an aria is a solo song in an opera

indicators.note: most of the word, without its last letter

parts.note: a zone is a region

explanation.surface: A state's region is largely the setting of an operatic number.
explanation.definitionFit: The south-western state containing the Grand Canyon, capital Phoenix.

clue.text: Address given weekly in advertiser monotonously

indicators.note: the word sits within the run of letters advertiser monotonously

explanation.surface: A weekly speech delivered in a flat drone by an advertiser.
explanation.definitionFit: A preacher's talk delivered at church each Sunday is an address given weekly.

clue.text: High-powered car, mostly refined and fast, producing commotion

indicators.note: most of the word but its final letter is used

parts.note: a turbo is a car with a turbocharged engine
U means upper-class, so socially refined
Lent is the Christian season of fasting

explanation.surface: A powerful, classy, speedy motor causing a stir.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fast' looks like speed but is the noun, a period of fasting: LENT. U for upper-class is an old British label.
explanation.definitionFit: Turbulent conditions are stormy and disorderly, full of disturbance and unrest.

clue.text: Criminal connection trapped hard fellow

indicators.note: the connection holds the hard letter caught inside it

parts.note: a tie is a link or bond
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A crook's associate has caught a tough guy.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who steals is a lawbreaker, a type of criminal.

clue.text: Stunning device underwent new testing on reflection

indicators.note: as in a mirror, the letters for underwent new testing appear backwards

parts.note: to resit an exam, past tense resat

explanation.surface: A dazzling gadget, retested and then reconsidered.
explanation.walkthrough: To resit is the British term for retaking an exam.
explanation.definitionFit: An electroshock weapon used by police to incapacitate someone temporarily.

clue.text: Wash nightwear in separated clothing

indicators.note: to clothe is to cover, so the words nightwear in separated wrap round the answer

explanation.surface: Laundering pyjamas inside the separated garments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is part of the text, not a signal; 'clothing' is a verb wrapping the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To rinse is to wash out lightly with clean water.

clue.text: Philosopher's style becoming a bugbear

parts.note: John Stuart Mill was a British philosopher, giving Mill's
tone means manner or style

explanation.surface: A thinker's way of writing is turning into a nuisance.
explanation.definitionFit: A burden or persistent source of trouble, as in a weight round one's neck, is a bugbear.

clue.text: Carbon material? It's used for drawing

parts.note: C is the chemical symbol for carbon
rayon is a synthetic fabric

explanation.surface: Carbon as a medium for drawing pictures, like charcoal.
explanation.definitionFit: A stick of coloured wax used by children to draw pictures.

clue.text: Scold a Republican infiltrating English party

indicators.note: a Republican gets inside the English party

parts.note: a bash is a party

explanation.surface: An American politician crashes a British party and gets a telling-off.
explanation.walkthrough: An Australian informal word for haranguing someone at length.
explanation.definitionFit: To talk at someone relentlessly, nagging or berating them, is to scold.
